hourly.title: Hourly
hourly.chartHint: Hourly chart. Hover, tap or drag to read values.

humidity.title: Humidity
humidity.para1: Relative humidity is how much water vapour the air holds compared with the most it could hold at that temperature.
humidity.para2: Dew point is the temperature the air would need to cool to for humidity to reach 100%. It is the better guide to how sticky it feels: below {comfortable} is comfortable, above {muggy} feels muggy.

wind.title: Wind
wind.para1: Strongest today: {speed} {unit}. Speeds are averages 10 m above the ground; gusts are short bursts that can be much stronger.
wind.para2: The arrow shows where the wind is blowing to. The direction named, like NNW, is where it is coming from.

precip.title: Precipitation
precip.unlikely: Rain is unlikely in the next 24 hours
precip.para1: Precipitation is any water falling from clouds: rain, drizzle, hail or snow. The total is the depth it would leave on flat ground.
precip.para2: Bars show the expected amount for each two-hour slot; the percentage is the highest chance of rain in that slot.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.lowest: Lowest in the next 24 h: {value} {unit} around {time}
visibility.staying: Staying clear for the next 24 hours
visibility.para1: Visibility is the distance at which you can clearly see a prominent object, like a building or hill, against the sky.
visibility.para2: Rain, fog, dust, smoke and haze all reduce it. Below 1 km counts as fog; below 5 km, drive with your lights on.

pressure.title: Pressure
pressure.steady: Little change over the next 3 hours
pressure.para1: Air pressure is the weight of the atmosphere above you. Tidy shows mean sea-level pressure, so places at different heights can be compared; about 1013 hPa is average.
pressure.para2: Falling pressure often brings cloud, wind or rain. Rising pressure usually means calmer, clearer weather.

uv.title: UV index

low.advice: Little protection needed. Sunglasses on bright days.

moderate.advice: Hat, sunglasses and SPF 30+ sunscreen. Seek shade around midday.

high.advice: Protection essential. Cut time in the sun between 11 AM and 3 PM.

veryHigh.advice: Extra protection. Avoid the midday sun, cover up and reapply sunscreen.

extreme.advice: Unprotected skin can burn in minutes. Stay in shade at midday.

uv.para: The UV index measures the strength of the sun’s ultraviolet radiation, from 0 to 11+. It peaks around midday, and clouds block less of it than you might think.

airQuality.title: Air quality

advice.good: Air quality is good. A fine time to be outside.
advice.moderate: Acceptable for most people. If you are unusually sensitive to air pollution, consider cutting back on long or hard exertion outdoors.
advice.sensitive: People with heart or lung conditions, older adults and children should reduce long or hard exertion outdoors.
advice.unhealthy: Everyone may start to feel effects. Sensitive groups should avoid long or hard exertion outdoors.
advice.veryUnhealthy: Health alert: everyone should limit time outdoors, and sensitive groups should stay inside.
advice.hazardous: Emergency conditions. Everyone should avoid outdoor activity.

airQuality.para1: The US EPA index rates the air from 1 (Good) to 6 (Hazardous), based on whichever pollutant is worst right now.
airQuality.para2: PM2.5 and PM10 are fine particles from smoke, dust and traffic. O₃ is ground-level ozone, which builds up on hot, sunny afternoons.

about.intro: Tidy shows the weather where you are — right now, hour by hour, and the next few days — without an account, ads or a setup flow. Here is what each panel on that screen is for.

now.body: Tidy asks once for your location and opens on it: temperature, what it actually feels like, chance of rain, humidity, pressure and visibility. Search any city to look somewhere else.

hours.body: Summary lays the day out as hour cards — temperature, rain, wind, and when the sun rises or sets. Trends plots temperature, feels-like, rain, wind or humidity as a curve you can tap or drag to read.

week.body: Highs, lows and rain chance for the next three days, on one shared scale so warmer days really look warmer. Pick a day and the rest of the screen follows it.

night.body: How long until sunset or the next moonrise, how much daylight there is, and tonight’s moon phase — counted in the city’s own time, wherever you are looking from.

air.body: Air quality and UV index, read back as plain words instead of raw index numbers: good, moderate, unhealthy. Worth a look before a long run or an afternoon outside.

about.settingsNote: Tidy also speaks বাংলা, switches between °C and °F, and follows your system’s light or dark theme. Change any of it from Settings.

tides.cardLabel: Tides at {name}: {trend}, {level} {unit} now. {next}. Open tide times
tides.inland: {place} is inland, so these are the tides at {name}, the nearest station ({km} km away).

none.title: No tide station nearby
none.body: The nearest one is more than 300 km away. Tides matter on coasts and tidal rivers.

moon.title: Moon & tides
moon.notSoon: Not in the next few weeks
moon.explain: Tides run biggest a day or two after a new or full moon, when the sun and moon pull in line, and smallest near the quarter moons.

leads.semidiurnal: {name} has two high and two low tides a day, of about the same height, about 50 minutes later each day.
leads.mixedSemidiurnal: {name} has two high and two low tides most days, but one of each pair is noticeably bigger than the other.
leads.mixedDiurnal: {name} often has just one high and one low tide a day, with a smaller second tide on some days.
leads.diurnal: {name} has one high and one low tide a day.

footer.disclaimer: Tide times are astronomical predictions from harmonic constants. Wind, air pressure and river flow can move the real water level, so don't use them for navigation.
